record.original_question: Let 2 < p < ∞, and let X be a subspace of an L^p space that does not contain a copy of ℓ^p(ω_1). Must there exist a finite measure μ such that X embeds into L^p(μ)?

evidence.quote: Problem 1.2 (Johnson-Schechtman, [73]). Let 2 < p < ∞ and let X be a subspace of an L^p space such that X does not contain ℓ^p(ω_1). Does X embed into L^p(μ) for some finite measure μ?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $2 < p < \infty$. Let $X$ be a (closed) infinite-dimensional Banach space that is isomorphic to a subspace of $L^p(\nu)$ for some (possibly non-$\sigma$-finite) measure $\nu$. Assume that $X$ does not contain an isomorphic copy of $\ell^p(\omega_1)$, where $\ell^p(\omega_1)$ denotes the Banach space of $p$-summable families indexed by the first uncountable ordinal $\omega_1$. Must there exist a finite measure $\mu$ such that $X$ is isomorphic to a subspace of $L^p(\mu)$?
artifact.status_search_result: The analogous statement for $1 < p < 2$ was established by Johnson and Schechtman ("Subspaces of $L_p$ that embed into $L_p(\mu)$ with $\mu$ finite", Israel J. Math., 2014), exploiting the fact (Enflo–Rosenthal) that $\ell_p(\aleph_1)$ does not embed into $L_p(\mu)$ for $\mu$ finite when $1<p<2$. For the range $2<p<\infty$ the question remains the natural counterpart and no resolution was located in the literature; the problem appears to still be open.

status_evidence.title: Subspaces of L_p that embed into L_p(µ) with µ finite
status_evidence.snippet: If X is a subspace of an L_p space, 1 < p < 2, and ℓ_p(ℵ_1) does not embed into X, then X embeds into L_p(µ) for some finite measure µ.
status_evidence.claim: The companion case 1 < p < 2 is solved affirmatively; the case 2 < p < ∞ is the remaining problem.
